observation: Round 1 (inter_radius 0.07; binary_threshold 115; oblique Hough 45/gap 60; horizontal Hough 40) moved the proxy only 0.6763 -> 0.6806 (correspondence_f1@15 0.4117 -> 0.4194, fill rate flat 0.745, NaN flat 0.109, ring_count_error 0). The round-1 artifacts explain why the detection knobs were nearly inert: (1) the binarised outlier map is unchanged because the outlier depth image is written with vmin/vmax from the denoise radius band [2.32, 2.79], so intensity 127 corresponds to r ~ 2.54 while every outlier pixel lies in r = 2.586-2.790 (5th percentile 2.750) - any binary_threshold in [100, 160] keeps ~all pixels, i.e. the knob is dead on this scan; (2) only 1789 interpolated joint points were added (outliers are capped 16205 -> 2800 before pairwise interpolation), so inter_radius has tiny leverage; (3) the 10 verticals are already synthetic ring-centre lines ('No vertical lines detected -> fallback'), so ring count is pinned regardless of Hough settings; (4) detected_lines.png is essentially identical to the anchor: ring 1 upper K still has no oblique pair ('assume'), ring 9 only a negative-slope line, and horizontal joints are still ~15 short segments. The decisive clue is in the outlier-map statistics: the outlier radii pile up against the denoise upper gate (max = 2.7899966 = mask_r_high, 75th pct 2.781, 95th 2.788) while the lining surface sits near r ~ 2.775. Joint/recess points are deeper (larger r) than the surface, and depth_threshold_high = 0.015 needs up to 15 mm of depth headroom, but the gate leaves only ~15 mm above the surface, so the deepest and most diagnostic joint points are being deleted in stage 2 before they can ever reach the outlier map, the Hough stage, or the SAM depth input. This is also consistent with the T1/T2 prior radius_range outer = 2.80 being above the current 2.79.
rule: sam4tun_ontology inter_stage_dependencies: stage_2_denoise.f_over_gate -> stage_3 joint evidence loss -> stage_4_detection.f_missing_lines (r_relax_hough precondition says rule out upstream causes first); remediation r_radial_gate_widen: 'widen [r_inner, r_outer] toward prior radius_range' (T1/T2 prior outer 2.80 >= current 2.79, bound allows up to 2.90). experiences.md section 7 tuning order: band selection (stage 3 in the order) must be validated before detection, and section 3 says the joint contrast in the depth map is what drives detection on T1/T2-like scans; the depth thresholds are out of bounds, so the radial gate is the only bounded lever that changes how many deep joint points survive. experiences section 5: verticals are synthetic here, so line count == ring count is guaranteed and the change cannot break ring_count_error.
failure_mode: stage_2_denoise.f_over_gate on the upper radial bound (mask_r_high clips the recessed joint points), propagating to stage_3_upsample.f_joint_oversmoothed (thin joint evidence, especially in the low-density left third of the map) and stage_4_detection.f_missing_lines (assumed prompt in ring 1, single-sided prompt in ring 9, sparse horizontal joints -> low correspondence_f1@15).
rationale: Widen only the upper radial gate: denoising.mask_r_high 2.79 -> 2.85 (+6 cm of headroom; prior outer 2.80, bound 2.90). This retains joint/recess points that are 15-75 mm deeper than the lining so enhance_outlier_points can flag them (depth_threshold_high 0.015 becomes reachable), which should thicken the joint lines in the binary map for both oblique (K) and horizontal (B/A) joints and sharpen joint contrast in the SAM depth input so mask edges land on the joints - the direct route to a higher correspondence_f1@15. mask_r_low stays 2.32 (rails/floor side unchanged). Keep the detection stage permissive so the extra joint evidence can be used: hough_threshold_oblique 40 (bound), maxLineGap_oblique 80 (bound) to bridge the dotted K joints in rings 0/1/9, hough_threshold_horizontal 40; keep inter_radius 0.07. Drop binary_threshold (dead knob on this scan, shown above). Ring count is pinned by the synthetic verticals, so the main risk is retaining out-of-band noise behind the lining (depth_outlier_ratio and NaN may shift slightly) and, if the widened band lets grout holes/bolt pockets act as extra 'joints', spurious oblique lines - the [6,9] deg angle filter and the K-row pattern gate limit that. Expected: correspondence_f1@15 up clearly (>0.45), det_fallback_ratio 0.1 -> 0.0 if ring 1 gets its oblique pair, denoise_retained_ratio slightly up, NaN flat or down, ring_count_error 0. If round 2 shows depth_outlier_ratio ballooning or the proxy dropping, round 3 should pull mask_r_high back to ~2.81 rather than revisit Hough.
